answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns. Courtship is an event with no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship has no player turns or listed turn effects.

answers.answer: Host in order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve round event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose an activity tile; play the exact required gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; clean up by sending used servants to Expended Service and played gentry to personal discard, returning the activity tile to its tableau column and flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the round marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, ‘Hosting an activity’ steps 1–8.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; round-track event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. The two passing benefits are £200 or the free Market refresh. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh’.

answers.answer: Yes. The PR6 activity and PR6 guests pass screening because screening uses reputation fixed at the end of step 2, when you are at 6.1. You may then use four Service Help actions, provided you can pay each cost; the later drop to 3.4 does not invalidate screening. Each Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, never directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2; later changes do not invalidate. Service Help moves one servant from Quarters to Available for 3 increments.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours, with choice of order within each group. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss; negative reputation can fall only to 1.1, and positives must resolve first. A money penalty must be fully payable, using positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if still unable to fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 and ‘A money penalty must be fully payable.’

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gives £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant and moves one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; this special action is once per turn. At minimum reputation 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: Host the Servant Hiring activity with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, and put them in Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. On first use the room upgrades. Its upgraded side instead permits recruiting one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, instead of hiring up to two from supply; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: ‘Butler’s Room’ paragraph.

answers.answer: A housekeeper can substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman can substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler can substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman) even when that type is still available.
answers.evidence: ‘Servants and hiring’ substitution rules.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry, which takes one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Quarters at your next service rotation and to Available at your second subsequent rotation; passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier, and once in Quarters Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can allow earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: ‘Butler’s Pantry’ paragraph.

answers.answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot go below £100. You may never acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so you may buy above your reputation.
answers.evidence: ‘Builders’ Market and Reserve’: price, minimum, duplicate and reputation rules.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. If a draw duplicates a tile already in the Market, stack it there and draw again. If multiple spaces are filled, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Reserve-eligible tiles go directly to Reserve and another tile is drawn. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it does not trigger a refill.
answers.evidence: ‘Refill’ paragraph under Builders’ Market and Reserve.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; thereafter newly drawn Service tiles go directly to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement, is standard in this scope.
answers.evidence: ‘Open Reserve’ and ‘Refresh’ paragraphs; Overview says full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships 1–3, return both Fairchild cards to Alderley Hall. Score the current theme by summing printed VP of tiles in its current face-up category, including negative tile VP. The high scorer gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild; on a tie each tied player draws one VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Every player discards one objective; simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Seasonal upkeep then passes first player anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: ‘Courtship and seasonal upkeep’, steps 1–4 and following seasonal order.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds as usual, then score all four revealed themes (a category revealed twice counts twice, including negative VP). The high scorer gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Ties are broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied players draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players may take a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before moving the marker to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: ‘Final courtship (round 16)’ paragraph.

answers.answer: Final VP comes from improvement tiles (including negative printed VP); gentry in hand and discard (including family, negatives, and final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation levels 1–7 for 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; £1 per £200, rounded down; and retained VP cards’ printed VP. Highest total wins. Ties go to the player with the final Fairchild, then highest reputation level; if still tied, players share victory. Wheel position is irrelevant to ordinary reputation VP and ties.
answers.evidence: ‘Final VP’ table and paragraph; wheel position never breaks a final tie.

answers.answer: Normally you get five objectives at setup plus two on round 6, discard one at each of four courtships, and score the three remaining. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase your retained final count and do not cause an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: ‘Objectives and VP cards’ paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card’s benefit can be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused VP cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both a card’s benefit and its final VP.
answers.evidence: ‘A VP card offers a choice’ paragraph.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded after later uses. Buying alone does not flip it. A hybrid starts with the underlined icon up and flips after every use, moving to the newly face-up category; only that face-up category counts for courtship and objectives. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite each host their front activity once, then upgrade into monuments and cannot host again.
answers.evidence: ‘Improvements and ongoing effects’ and Special Rules & Edge Cases.

answers.answer: Resolve monument and Servants’ Hall effects in the ongoing-effects step after the round event, both when hosting and passing (step 2 hosting; step 3 passing). Each monument gives one reputation per ordinary turn, not during courtship; newly purchased monuments first pay on a later turn. Servants’ Hall uses any one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant goes to Expended Service at turn end and cannot also serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: ‘Improvements and ongoing effects’; event order in hosting and passing.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with that guest’s normal service; it doubles all guest favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand with normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve the others normally, then it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, not negative ones, keep the guest and put it in discard at cleanup, then it upgrades into a monument. Each has a fixed count of one guest that cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following fixed-count paragraph.

answers.answer: A random player gets the first-player marker. Starting with that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose an available base family board. Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Stack the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at the bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. After family bonuses, Cavendish starts at 1.4 and the other families at 1.1. Each player gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starter tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money, £300.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5.

answers.answer: For three players, stock Servants for Hire with three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers or housekeepers.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player’s hand; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests remain casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules, not a separate guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4 and ‘Gentry, screening, dismissal and family’.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five monuments. You may select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles go into the draw bag; tiles that later upgrade into monuments also go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Draw until there are six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack eligible duplicates in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort six spaces by ascending sorting number starting at £300. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments cannot enter the opening Market.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme, so the first courtship is open, and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. Old revealed themes remain; final courtship uses all four.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; final courtship scores all four revealed themes.

answers.answer: At hosting-turn rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available Service first. The servant in Expended Service then moves to Quarters, each advancing only one space. An available servant you do not use remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: Quarters to Available first, then Expended to Quarters; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No. Village Fair is resolved before choosing/hosting an activity; if the Private Study is not already upgraded at that event step, it gives no reward that turn. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Village Fair table: upgraded Study reward on spaces 3 and 9; no reward if not upgraded at this step.

answers.answer: Resolve the round-track event before ongoing effects: after service rotation on a hosting turn, or after servants and discarded gentry return on a pass. At space 6, draw two objectives and keep both secret with your other objectives. The event applies on each player’s turn, including passing players.
answers.evidence: Round-track events section says all players’ turns follow the same timing; space 6 draws two, kept secret.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so low-reputation players may use higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events, space 14; all other requirements including service and gentry remain.

answers.answer: During Builders’ Holiday you may buy any number of tiles from Market and/or Reserve within your funds, at the prices that applied before the sequence. Finish all purchases from that single unchanged market before sliding/refilling; buying earlier tiles does not change later tiles’ prices. Do not refresh between purchases by special action or VP card. The same single-unchanged-market and no-refresh-between-purchases rule applies to Market Purchase VP cards; refill resulting empty spaces together afterward.
answers.evidence: ‘Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card’ paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while refilling all six spaces under normal refill rules; they cannot reappear during that refresh. After the refill, return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Reserve tiles stay unchanged.
answers.evidence: ‘Refresh’: leave Reserve unchanged, set all Market tiles aside, refill, then return them to bag.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers a level. Minimum is 1.1 and standard maximum is 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; special actions can be taken before or during a reputation favour to make space.
answers.evidence: ‘Reputation, wealth and special actions’ reputation arithmetic and maximum rules.

answers.answer: Money is public. Players may not give or receive money between them. You may never spend more than you have. The common money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Money held is public; no transfers; never spend more than held; supply is unlimited.

answers.answer: For a ladies requirement, female family members or female guests count; for gentlemen, male family members or male guests count. A casual-guest requirement requires casual guests and excludes family, and family requirements accept only family. You must play exactly the printed number and types, with no extra gentry. Family has no PR and needs no personal service.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4: exact gentry types/counts; ladies/gentlemen definitions; family screening/service rule.

answers.answer: An ordinary guest-invite favour draws the indicated guest card, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to your hand. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand. Put rejected screened cards on the bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: ‘Invite Guest favour’ and screening guests paragraphs.

answers.answer: Dismissal is always optional, so you need not dismiss if you have no unwanted guests. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including a guest just drawn earlier during Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the dismissed guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Dismissal paragraph under ‘Gentry, screening, dismissal and family’.

answers.answer: Lord: gain £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: gain both £100 and one reputation. Thus Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits; Lord has a single benefit.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: The Young Lady always draws one casual guest. Her extra two-reputation admirer bonus applies only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity: not a male casual guest, not a female prestige guest, but yes for Charles Fairchild, who is male prestige.
answers.evidence: Young Lady row and Charles Fairchild ruling.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither is a family card; both may be dismissed under the normal optional guest-dismissal rule.
answers.evidence: Fairchild paragraph: both prestige, no PR; gender/service; Charles gives three reputation; Elizabeth gives both favours; both dismissible.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent’s reputation by two and makes you lose one reputation yourself. A player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section gives the gossip effects; reputation rule protects players at minimum.

answers.answer: The Barn gives one reputation every time you host an Estate activity. It gives nothing merely for owning an Estate tile and nothing when passing.
answers.evidence: Barn paragraph under ‘Improvements and ongoing effects’.

answers.answer: Ordinary hosting rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each and without reputation cost. The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation in addition to Available Service; that servant goes to Expended Service at turn end and costs no reputation. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatably; it cannot take from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile paragraph and service mechanism table.

answers.answer: The front-side Private Study requires two family and a butler and has no tile favour. It upgrades after first use into an ongoing tile, so you do not host it repeatedly; its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds (spaces 3 and 9) without hosting or staffing it again.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph and Village Fair table.

answers.answer: Before upgrading, Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. After upgrading, it uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; extra objectives do not cause extra discard.

answers.answer: The Objective VP-card benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. The kept card adds one to your retained objective count; it does not cause an extra discard.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including servants in Expended Service, and they are usable immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available; it cannot move directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table, Refresh Service entry; Service Help comparison.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It does not make the servant immediately usable through hiring alone; it must be refreshed to Available (for example, by Refresh Service) before normal use.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Hire Servant destination; Refresh Service moves servants to Available.

answers.answer: Refresh Guest can return one gentry card, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If used before attendee selection, the returned card may be played at this activity if it meets the normal requirements; returning it does not automatically make it attend. It cannot return a card from hand or the current activity because its source is discard.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service VP is 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP table.

answers.answer: Both upgraded Queen’s Suite (Estate) and Lionheart Suite (Prestige) count as monuments for the monument objective and also retain their tile categories, so they count for the relevant Estate or Prestige category objective. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monument status does not replace category; hybrid rule.

answers.answer: Nature Group is worth 11 VP and requires Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is worth 12 VP and requires Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Owning the listed tiles at game end suffices; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference group list and ownership rule.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective counts prestige guests; a final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests, including casual and prestige guests, and awards 1 VP per complete group of three; an incomplete group scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: prestige guests include final Fairchild; one VP per complete three guests, all nonfamily.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on level (levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28), not wheel position; reputation tie resolution also uses level only.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP table; wheel position has no effect.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded, it draws one prestige guest. Upgraded, it draws one prestige guest and may optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottoms of their appropriate decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace paragraph under ‘Other base activity tiles’.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal-discard limit. Gentry in your discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to your hand.
answers.evidence: ‘Gentry, screening, dismissal and family’: no limit; discard-pile gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one of them, including one underneath another in a stack; you are not limited to the top tile. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: ‘Open Reserve’ paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to host an activity or pass; you do not have to host just because you can. If the preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you may take the free Market refresh benefit, also pay for the special-action refresh, and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards on the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action Refresh Market; passing and VP-card refreshes have separate availability. Buying multiple tiles under a Market Purchase VP card requires finishing purchases before any refresh.
answers.evidence: Special-action refresh limit and separate refresh methods; market purchase timing restriction.

answers.answer: No. Special actions are available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing, not during another player’s turn. You may take them before or even in the middle of resolving a reputation favour to create space.
answers.evidence: Special actions are available ‘at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing’.

answers.answer: No. Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional, so a printed guest-invite favour must be resolved even if you would rather not draw; you still resolve the other favours in the required order. An optional dismissal is different: it may be declined, and dismissal never is mandatory.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: favours mandatory unless expressly optional; dismissal is always optional.
